issues.body: `newest_concluded_run` examines only `unconfirmed[:NON_VERDICT_PROBE_CAP]` and then returns the older non-cancelled verdict. Therefore, if the first cancelled run that created jobs is the 11th candidate above an older `action_required` run, the function publishes that stale rejection even though the newer job-bearing run proves ingestion recovered. The new `_cancel_storm` assertion explicitly expects this false alarm (`id == "60"`) when run 101 has four jobs, so the prior round's correctness defect remains for a bounded but supported input. Rate-limit pressure can justify limiting requests, but it cannot turn unexamined newer evidence into affirmative evidence that the older rejection is current.
issues.fix_hint: After exhausting the probe budget without finding a job-bearing cancellation, do not promote the older rejection as current while additional unconfirmed candidates remain. Represent the lane as indeterminate/unreadable (with an always-emitted census state and recovery-hold behavior as appropriate), or obtain bounded bulk evidence that adjudicates all newer candidates. Replace the current cancel-storm expectation with an anti-vacuity assertion that the older rejection is not emitted when an unprobed newer cancellation may have executed jobs.
issues.title: The probe cap can still resurrect a stale rejection after recovery

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The revision now distinguishes ordinary pre-job cancellations from cancelled runs that executed jobs, wires that distinction through `fetch_lanes`, and adds a strong end-to-end regression test for the prior finding. However, the fixed probe cap deliberately recreates the same stale-rejection false alarm whenever the first job-bearing cancelled run is more than ten candidate cancellations deep. The included cancel-storm test confirms that behavior rather than preventing it. Because a newer run with jobs remains positive ingestion evidence regardless of its position in the sampled listing, the change is still incomplete and requires changes.
